questions.q: Which of the following is a stated benefit of having an Enterprise Architecture?
o: It eliminates the need for project management
It increases return on existing investment and reduces the risk of future investment
It removes the need for governance
questions.e: Benefits of EA include increased return on existing investment, reduced risk of future investment, more efficient operations, and better strategic decision making.

questions.q: Why is TOGAF considered suitable as an EA framework?
o: It is a rigid, one-size-fits-all process
It is generic, best-practice, and must be tailored to the enterprise
It applies only to IT service management
It is proprietary to a single vendor
questions.e: TOGAF is a generic, community-developed, best-practice framework that must be tailored. It can be used standalone or integrated with frameworks like ITIL, COBIT, and PRINCE2.

questions.q: Which architecture domain provides the blueprint for individual applications, their interactions, and their relationships to core business processes?
questions.e: The Application Architecture provides a blueprint for individual applications, their interactions, and their relationships to core business processes.

questions.q: The Enterprise Continuum is best described as which of the following?
o: A categorization for assets held in the enterprise repositories, from generic to specific
A list of stakeholders and concerns
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum is a categorization for assets in the enterprise repositories, explaining how generic solutions are leveraged and specialized for the organization.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository records decision logs, compliance assessments, and capability assessments?
questions.e: The Governance Repository holds the record of governance activity, including decision logs, compliance assessments, and capability assessments.

questions.q: What does the Enterprise Metamodel define, and where is it customized?
o: The migration schedule; customized in Phase F
The entities and their relationships within the enterprise; customized in the Preliminary Phase
The stakeholder map; customized in Phase A
The risk levels; customized in Phase E
questions.e: The Enterprise Metamodel defines the enterprise's entities and their relationships. It is enterprise-specific and customized in the Preliminary Phase as part of tailoring the framework.

questions.q: According to the four purpose capabilities, which one has the narrowest breadth, most detailed depth, and supports deployment of a single project?
questions.e: Support Solution Delivery has very narrow breadth (one project), the most detailed depth, and supports change governance and deployment for that project.

questions.q: Which pair correctly names two of the effect categories in TOGAF's risk classification scheme?
questions.e: Effect categories are catastrophic, critical, marginal, and negligible. Frequent and seldom are frequency categories; initial and residual are risk levels.

questions.q: In how many of the architecture domains can gaps occur?
questions.e: Gaps occur in all four domains. Gap analysis is used in almost all ADM phases to state what must change between baseline and target.

questions.q: How many documents make up the Fundamental Content of the TOGAF Standard, and how many are dedicated to the ADM?
o: Six documents, three dedicated to the ADM
Four documents, two dedicated to the ADM
Ten documents, five dedicated to the ADM
Six documents, one dedicated to the ADM
questions.e: The Fundamental Content has six documents; three of them (ADM, ADM Techniques, Applying the ADM) are dedicated to the ADM because it is the heart of the standard.

questions.q: Who directs and controls the EA team and the implementers during architecture work?
questions.e: The EA team and implementers are directed and controlled by the stakeholders. Governance ensures the work moves toward the agreed target.

questions.q: Which factors most commonly limit the scope of an architecture?
o: People, finance, objectives, stakeholder concerns, and the EA team's organizational authority
The version of the TOGAF Standard
questions.e: Scope is mostly limited by people, finance, objectives, stakeholder concerns, and the organizational authority of the EA team.

questions.q: Why does the TOGAF Standard recommend considering architecture alternatives?
o: To increase the number of deliverables
Because there can be multiple valid target architectures, and presenting alternatives surfaces trade-offs, hidden agendas, and new requirements
To avoid having to identify stakeholders
questions.e: Multiple valid targets may conform to the vision and principles. Presenting alternatives builds understanding of trade-offs and can surface hidden agendas, new principles, or requirements.

questions.q: Which of the following is defined in the Preliminary Phase and provides general rules and guidelines that endure over time?
questions.e: Architecture principles are general rules and guidelines defined in the Preliminary Phase; they are enduring and seldom amended.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of Phase A, Architecture Vision?
o: Finalize the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan
Define scope, identify stakeholders, and create the Architecture Vision
Perform architecture compliance reviews of the build
questions.e: Phase A defines scope, identifies stakeholders, creates the Architecture Vision, and obtains approval to proceed.

questions.q: An Application Communication Diagram is an artifact produced in which ADM phase?
questions.e: The Application Communication Diagram is an Application Architecture artifact produced in Phase C (Information Systems Architectures).

questions.q: In which ADM phase is a business value assigned to each work package?
questions.e: Assigning a business value to each work package is step 10.3.2, an explicit step of Phase F: Migration Planning. The Roadmap is first created in Phase E but business value assignment is confirmed in Phase F.

questions.q: Which deliverable is created in Phase F to enable architecture governance within implementation projects?
questions.e: The Implementation Governance Model is created in Phase F (tailoring an existing model if present) and applied in Phase G.

questions.q: In Phase G, which document is one of the simplest means to ensure an implementation conforms to the target architecture?
questions.e: The Architecture Contract is one of the simplest means to ensure the implementation conforms to the target architecture, realized through effective governance in Phase G.

questions.q: Phase H is often called a 'holding phase.' What does that mean?
o: It halts all architecture activity permanently
It keeps the ADM running and monitors for changes that may trigger an update or a new cycle
It holds the budget for future projects
It stores deliverables in the repository
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase that keeps the ADM running, managing change to the new architecture and deciding whether a change is a light update or warrants a new ADM cycle.

questions.q: In step 6 of ADM Requirements Management, where is the decision made to implement a changed requirement or defer it to a later ADM cycle?
o: In the Requirements Management process alone
questions.e: Step 6 assigns the implementation-or-deferral decision to the relevant ADM phase, together with assessing impacts and issuing Requirements Impact Assessment version n+1. Requirements Management records and coordinates changes and generates an impact assessment in step 5.

questions.q: Which of the following is a purpose of architecture principles?
o: To form the basis for future architecture decisions and enable decisions in trade-offs
To store artifacts in the repository
questions.e: Architecture principles form the basis for future architecture decisions, enable decision-making in trade-offs, align the enterprise, support governance, and reflect values.

questions.q: Which section of an architecture principle template answers the question 'how does this affect me?' by stating requirements, resources, costs, and activities?
questions.e: Implications state the requirements, resources, costs, and activities needed to carry out the principle, answering 'how does this affect me?'.

questions.q: A principle that allows balanced, flexible interpretation without contradictions satisfies which criterion?
questions.e: Consistent means the principle allows balanced, flexible interpretation without contradictions among principles.

questions.q: A business scenario distinguishes two kinds of actors. Which pair is correct?
questions.e: A business scenario contains human actors (who provide capabilities) and computer actors (which support capabilities), along with the problem, environment, and desired outcomes.

questions.q: In the Gap Analysis matrix, what is recorded at the intersection of an ABB that exists in both the baseline and the target?
questions.e: An ABB present in both the baseline and the target is marked 'included' at the intersection. A target ABB absent from the baseline is 'new'; a baseline ABB absent from the target is 'eliminated'.

questions.q: Which of these is the correct order of the risk management activities in TOGAF?
o: Identify, classify, initial assessment, mitigate, residual assessment, monitor
Classify, identify, initial assessment, mitigate, residual assessment, monitor
questions.e: The six activities in order are: risk classification, risk identification, initial risk assessment, risk mitigation and residual risk assessment, then risk monitoring and governance. Classification precedes identification.

questions.q: Which Series Guide covers using the TOGAF Standard in the Digital Enterprise?
o: G217, Using the TOGAF Standard in the Digital Enterprise
The Leader's Guide to Establishing an EA Capability
questions.e: Series Guide G217, Using the TOGAF Standard in the Digital Enterprise, is new in TOGAF 10 and covers digital enterprise support.

questions.q: How do multiple segment architectures relate to a strategic architecture?
o: They cover a smaller area than the strategic architecture
Together they cover the same area as the strategic architecture, at more detail
They are unrelated to the strategic architecture
questions.e: Multiple segment architectures together cover the same area as the strategic architecture but at more detail; multiple capability architectures detail a segment.

questions.q: How many defined owning teams should a single architecture partition ultimately have?
o: As many as the org chart requires
questions.e: Each partition has defined boundaries and one owning team; you partition until each architecture has a single owning team.

questions.q: Which scoping dimension determines which of business, data, application, and technology are in scope?
questions.e: The Architecture Domains dimension determines which of the four domains are in scope. The others are Breadth, Depth, and Time Period.

questions.q: Which of the following is a value delivered by architecture governance, per the notes?
questions.e: The value of governance includes discipline, responsibility, accountability, fairness, transparency, and independency.

questions.q: The Architecture Board is best described as which of the following?
o: A cross-organizational body of key architecture stakeholders responsible for review and maintenance of the EA
questions.e: The Architecture Board is a cross-organizational body of key architecture stakeholders (usually executives) responsible for the review and maintenance of the EA.

questions.q: The Business Users Architecture Contract is created at the end of which phase?
questions.e: The Business Users / Business Stakeholders Architecture Contract is created at the end of Phase F with the agreed plan and is also used in Phase H.

questions.q: In the Architecture Compliance process, which roles does the architect perform?
questions.e: During compliance review the architect acts as both auditor and advisor. The architect assesses the target; the stakeholders approve it.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a view and a viewpoint?
o: A view governs the construction of a viewpoint
Every view is rooted in a viewpoint, which governs the view's structure and content
A viewpoint is a specific instance of a view
questions.e: Every view is rooted in a viewpoint; the viewpoint is the generic lens that governs the structure and content of the specific view.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a well-defined building block?
o: It is tightly coupled to a single implementation
It is reusable, replaceable, and interoperates via a published, stable interface
It cannot evolve with technology or standards
questions.e: A good building block is reusable, replaceable, well specified, loosely coupled to its implementation, evolves with technology, and interoperates via a published, stable interface.

questions.q: Which deliverable shows the schedule of projects and the 'how' of reaching the target, aligned to the roadmap's level of detail?
questions.e: The Implementation and Migration Plan is the schedule of projects showing the 'how'; the Architecture Roadmap shows the 'what' on a timeline.

questions.q: What distinguishes an artifact from a deliverable in the TOGAF Standard?
o: An artifact is contractually specified and signed off; a deliverable describes one aspect
A deliverable is contractually specified and signed off; an artifact describes one aspect and deliverables contain artifacts
An artifact can only be a diagram; a deliverable can only be a catalog
questions.e: A deliverable is contractually specified, reviewed, and signed off; an artifact describes one aspect of the architecture. Deliverables contain artifacts (catalogs, matrices, diagrams).

questions.q: Which artifact class shows the relationships between things, such as a Capability/Organization Matrix?
questions.e: A matrix shows relationships between things. A catalog is a list of things; a diagram is a picture of things.
